g.text: added up once, by one thread
No shared writes, so no lock and no waiting.
Works when the data splits: arrays, ranges, independent requests.
a list: every node points at two others
One thread at a time between lock and unlock.
Needed when the data does not split: lists, trees, graphs, counters.
Partition what you can; synchronize what is left. The kernel does the same with its own shared data, on your behalf.
